name: SMEFT-Pheno-Agent
reason: arXiv:2607.22331 (v1, 2026-07-24, hep-ph) verified and matches: a natural-language AI agent coordinating a twelve-phase SMEFT collider-phenomenology workflow. Full source released under MIT at the authors' own GitHub (NBAlexis = author Ji-Chong Yang; repo created 2026-07-21, before submission) with a Gitee mirror the GitHub repo itself designates as the latest version. Multi-step scientific workflow, computational closure only.

record.name: SMEFT-Pheno-Agent
record.inputs: Natural-language SMEFT analysis intent; nine interactively collected configuration parameters locked into run_config.json
record.outputs: MadGraph5_aMC@NLO/Pythia/Delphes simulation samples, ML-based event selections, statistical constraints on Wilson coefficients, machine-readable phase manifests and prose drafts
record.notes: Twelve-phase Python workflow in which the agent proposes kinematic observables and ML algorithms while all numerics are delegated to validated domain tools; Phase 1 (configuration intake) is the only interactive stage and phases 2-12 then run unattended with physical parameters locked. Distributed as a portable skill under the Agent Skills open standard (MIT license; runtimes such as Codex or Claude Code listed as illustrative).

name: Lean-QuantumAlg-Bench / Lean-QIT-Bench
reason: arXiv:2607.21533 (v1, 2026-07-23, quant-ph) verified: two Lean 4 theorem-completion benchmarks (36 and 40 tasks) with deterministic proof checking and pre-assigned difficulty weights, evaluating four frontier models in a common theorem-proving agent framework. Both benchmark repos are linked from the paper, predate submission (created 2026-06-30 and 2026-06-22), and are Apache-2.0. Clear benchmark scope (B).

record.name: Lean-QuantumAlg-Bench / Lean-QIT-Bench
record.domain: Quantum algorithms and quantum information theory / formal theorem proving (Lean 4)
record.inputs: Lean 4 theorem-completion tasks (sorry-target statements with paired TeX statements and optional hints) compiling in a fixed environment
record.outputs: Machine-checked Lean proofs; difficulty-weighted scores from deterministic proof checking plus targeted semantic review; cost and completion-rate comparisons
record.notes: 36-task quantum-algorithm and 40-task quantum-information Lean 4 benchmarks with difficulty weights assigned before model execution; evaluates GPT-5.5, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4-Pro and MiniMax M3 in a common agent framework, with library-augmented deduction (access to a verified domain library) improving all eight model-benchmark comparisons. Repos (Apache-2.0) are published mirrors of the reviewed public benchmark surface.

name: IteraSim RAG
reason: Adjudication of the crowded-niche flag: this is a system, not a component. Beyond retrieval, it splits generation across Architect/InputWriter/Reviewer agents, compiles custom solvers via wmake, launches the OpenFOAM simulation, parses solver logs, and runs a corrective loop bounded to ten cycles - full NL-request-to-executed-case closure, functionally the same class as Foam-Agent/MetaOpenFOAM already in the catalog. arXiv:2607.20346 (v1, 2026-07-22) verified. Caveats carried in the record: single-author paper with disclosed financial interest; the engine/orchestrator is commercial IP available only on request, and only the 28-case benchmark kit is open (MIT, verified LICENSE text).

record.name: IteraSim RAG
record.domain: Computational fluid dynamics / OpenFOAM engineering simulation
record.inputs: Natural-language OpenFOAM CFD case requests (zero-shot setup, parameter modification, troubleshooting)
record.outputs: Complete mutually consistent OpenFOAM input decks (solver, discretisation, boundary-condition dictionaries); compiled and executed cases with log-driven Reviewer corrections
record.notes: Multi-stage RAG back-end (query expansion, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, MMR re-ranking, keyword router) feeding Architect/InputWriter/Reviewer agents over a canonical-knowledge layer; the Reviewer compiles, runs the simulation and iterates in a corrective loop bounded to ten cycles. The retrieval engine and orchestrator are commercial IP of IteraSim (single-author paper, disclosed financial interest) available for academic collaboration or licensing on request; only the 28-case benchmark, rubric and figure scripts are open (MIT, Zenodo-archived per paper).

name: Auto Research for Materials
reason: Adjudication of the methodology flag: this is a methodology paper, not an indexable system. arXiv:2607.17100 (v1 2026-07-19, v2 2026-07-29; cs.MA/cs.AI/cs.SE) verified and not withdrawn, but the contribution is 'intervention-centered Auto Research' - a validation protocol (axis-wise search with frozen winners plus outer-holdout auditing) for judging auto-research decisions, demonstrated in a single materials-ML case study with DeepSeek-V4-Pro as the executing agent. No named released system, and no code, data, or repository URL anywhere in the v2 full text (checked). Fails scope (method paper / one-off case study) and has no verifiable artifact; would need a named, released system to reconsider.

name: LQCDMaster
reason: arXiv:2607.15001 (v1, 2026-07-16, hep-lat/cs.AI/hep-ph) verified: tool-augmented, skill-guided agent converting natural-language lattice-QCD tasks into executable PyQUDA workflows, reproducing expert implementations at machine precision in 63/70 benchmark tasks. Source, skills, Wick-contraction tool and benchmark released at the SJTU authors' org repo (linked from paper, created 2026-07-07). README declares MIT twice but the repo contains no standalone LICENSE file as of 2026-08-13 - noted as a caveat, classified open-source on the explicit README grant.

record.name: LQCDMaster
record.domain: Lattice quantum chromodynamics / HPC scientific computing
record.outputs: Executable PyQUDA measurement scripts, Slurm job-submission artifacts, execution logs and numerical observables (two-point and three-point functions, Wilson loops)
record.notes: Planner-Executor agent pair with expert-annotated LQCD skills and a deterministic Wick-contraction tool (generate_einsum); a disclosed human checkpoint lets physicists review and refine the plan before execution, after which code generation, static analysis and auto-debugging proceed autonomously (GPT-5.4 primary backbone, DeepSeek-V4-Pro validation). Reproduces expert implementations at machine precision on 63 of 70 benchmark tasks; README declares MIT but the repo lacks a standalone LICENSE file as of 2026-08-13.

name: NNStar
reason: arXiv:2607.13930 (v1, 2026-07-15, nucl-th/astro-ph.HE/physics.comp-ph) verified: end-to-end agent automating RMF model construction, EoS building, TOV integration and Bayesian scoring for nuclear matter and neutron stars, delivered as a portable skill for the open agent platform openclaw. The paper links its own companion repo (skill + 100-task harness + data). Access downgraded to source-available: the repo's LICENSE file is a literal 'TODO: choose and confirm a license' placeholder, so the public code is unlicensed and cannot be called open-source; the harness also ran against a private remote machine, so paths need adaptation to reproduce.

record.name: NNStar
record.domain: Nuclear matter and neutron-star astrophysics / equation-of-state inference
record.inputs: RMF Lagrangian specifications with coupling parameters; natural-language task requests to the agent platform
record.outputs: Saturation properties, beta-equilibrium equation of state with crust matching, TOV mass-radius-tidal-deformability predictions, Bayesian joint-analysis scores against nuclear and astrophysical constraints
record.notes: Delivered not as a standalone program but as a self-describing skill (rmf-toolkit plus symbolic and numerical physics engines) installed into the open LLM agent platform openclaw; the paper states the agent can read a model, fit its parameters and report all observables without human intervention (computational closure only). Companion repo bundles the skill and a 100-task with/without-skill benchmark harness, but its LICENSE file is an unresolved placeholder (unlicensed as of 2026-08-13) and the harness targeted a private remote machine.
